A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AIM research, with matching authors, principal results, Algorithm 1, and Figures 1–5. All 39 pages of v1 and 41 pages of v2, including Appendices A–D, support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic-data experiments comparing AMP, Adam gradient descent, and averaged gradient descent with theoretical predictions, including appendix experiments in Figure 4.

after.justification: V2 retains these original numerical experiments and their reported outcomes in Figures 1, 2, and 4.

M1.justification: The stated deep-attention and seq2seq recursions now use explicitly centered logits, and Appendix B specifies a mean-aggregated multi-head variant previously only mentioned in a footnote. The general AIM framework, Algorithm 1, and averaged-GD estimator are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic Gaussian teacher–student settings with hardmax, softmax, and linear output channels. The expanded multi-head discussion introduces no evaluated dataset or test scenario.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain AMP, Adam GD, averaged GD, and Bayes-optimal predictions. The newly cited polynomial matrix-denoising approach is suggested but not evaluated.

E3.justification: The single-layer data-generation specification changes its diagonal subtraction from delta_ab to delta_ab Tr(S), correcting v1 Eq. (25) in v2 Eq. (27). This revises the written experimental specification to match the already-centered general AIM and loss; it does not establish reruns. Other reported settings are retained.

E4.justification: The width-limit analyses, token-number checks, and supplementary channel comparisons already appear in v1 Section 4 and Appendix D. V2 adds interpretation and mathematical derivations, without new ablations, robustness tests, or case studies.

E5.justification: Both versions retain 16-realization averaging and the same error-bar descriptions in Figures 1, 2, and 4. Appendix D.8 retains 32 optimization restarts for averaged GD and the same Monte Carlo estimation procedure.

E6.justification: All five figures retain identical plot content. The reported AMP agreement, averaged-GD versus GD findings, recovery trends, and approximately 0.563 hardmax weak-recovery threshold are unchanged. No numerical results accompany the multi-head extension.

T1.justification: Appendix B substantially revises the attention-to-AIM correspondence through centered transport identities and an explicit multi-head derivation. V2 also corrects the hardmax sign coding and the token summation bound in Result 3.2. However, the new multi-head derivation moves averaging through softmax between Eqs. (57) and (59), which is not generally valid.

C1.justification: The introduction now attributes empirical Bayes-optimal agreement specifically to averaged GD. It explicitly separates the supervised attention problem from full Transformer blocks and highlights the multi-head mapping. The central AIM, Bayes-optimality, and AMP contributions remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds classification-versus-regression interpretations of hardmax and softmax, asserts applicability of the rescaled predictions when T grows much slower than d, and suggests polynomial denoisers for multilayer AMP. It also clarifies the boundary between isolated attention learning and full Transformer training.

D1.justification: V2 identifies the centering expectation as an empirical average over input data and explicitly writes sample and token-pair indices and summations in the training loss. Appendix D.8 retains the same code access information, PyTorch version, Adam learning rate, and numerical implementation settings.

R1.justification: V2 adds Semerjian's work on low-degree polynomial matrix denoising and Bun et al.'s rotational invariant estimator paper to support the suggested denoising route. The broader positioning against finite-width attention theories is unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized notation and wording corrections, revises contribution statements, and expands explanations in Sections 1, 3, 4, and Appendix B. The overall section and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: Expanded equation displays and text reflow alter layout around Algorithm 1 and the references, and shift appendix figures to later pages. All five figures retain their plots, axes, legends, and structure; no figures or tables are added.

improvement.justification: V2 improves qualification of the AGD and attention-scope claims and corrects existing normalization and sign formulas. However, its new Appendix B multi-head derivation incorrectly replaces an average of softmax outputs with softmax of averaged logits. With the empirical evidence unchanged, these clarity and correction benefits coexist with unreliable added theoretical support, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
